name: Kami (Nigeria)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only sociolinguistic survey (Decker & Abraham 2022, SIL) and Nupoid comparative wordlists; no phonological description of Nigerian Kami found

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record kami1258 (Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist; no grammar, sketch or phonology refs; the attached Houghton 1897 'Kami Vocabularies' JRAS is Kami/Khumi of Burma, a mis-attached reference).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Decker, Ken and Benard Abraham. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Kami [kmi] Language of Niger State, Nigeria with Additional Observations on Nupe Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-021, 57 pp. Dallas: SIL International. (entry https://www.sil.org/resources/publications/entry/95076; PDF downloaded via the Internet Archive 20241110173832)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.3 'Phonetic inventory' pp.11-13 gives only a consonant and vowel inventory from a 222-item survey wordlist ('initial cursory observations'; 'Kami probably has a five-vowel system'); Appendix E p.39: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Zero occurrences of 'stress'/'accent'. Sec. 3 p.2 states the only prior linguistic information on Kami is Blench 1989/2013 (wordlists), CAPRO 1995, Weise 2013.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 237 Kami.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; entry gives location (Ebo town & 11 villages, Lapai LGA), population, classification, 'Source(s) Blench (1989)'; no Refs line listing any wordlist/grammar/phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2013. The Nupoid languages of West-Central Nigeria: overview and comparative wordlist. Working document, Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 141 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (0 hits). Item 9 'Kami' p.3: location, <=500 speakers, 'closely related to Gupa and Dibo and shows partial assimilation of the open vowels'. Sec. 2.3 Tone p.8, family-level: 'All Nupoid languages presently studied have at least five surface tones, three level tones and two glides.. these can all be analysed as three underlying level tones'. Kami appears only as a wordlist column.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kami language (Nigeria)' (stub citing Blench 2013 and Ethnologue 18).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Item 14 'Kami' (location, speakers); sec. 14.3.3 Tone pp.314-315: same family-level statement (three level tones + two glides; downdrift in Nupe, Gbari, Gade).

sources.citation: Weise, Constanze. 2013. Governance and Ritual Sovereignty at the Niger-Benue Confluence.. PhD dissertation, UCLA (ProQuest).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Listed by Glottolog and by Decker & Abraham as containing Kami lexical data; a history thesis, very unlikely to describe prosody, but the only other academic work with Kami material.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 1979-1982 field notes / Scholtz (1976) manuscript wordlists of Gupa, Kami, Dibo, Kakanda (cited in Blench 2013:1 as unpublished manuscript wordlists)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only other primary Kami data known (tone-marked manuscript wordlists underlying Blench's comparative list); would at most show tone marking, not a stress statement, but is the sole unpublished primary material.

sources.citation: Any University of Ilorin / Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida University (Lapai) BA/MA long essay on Kami (Ebbo) phonology, if one exists
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Nigerian departmental theses are the usual locus of first phonologies of small Niger State languages (cf. Oyebade 1988 on Kakanda); none is recorded for Kami in Glottolog, OLAC, Blench's Atlas or the 2022 SIL survey's literature review, so existence is unverified.
